image_description: A close-up, high-contrast image of a cooked Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) against a dark background. The crab is positioned ventral-side up or tilted, revealing the white/cream underside of the carapace and legs, while the dorsal side shows characteristic reddish-orange coloration from cooking. The large chelipeds (claws) are prominent with red tips and white joints. Several walking legs are visible extending laterally. The texture appears glossy and wet, typical of cooked shellfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the crab (ventral/tilted view) and the lighting obscure the anterior margin where eyes would be located; they are not clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portions of the carapace show the expected reddish-orange hue consistent with cooked Dungeness crab, and the surface appears smooth and convex.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While cooking alters the color to orange/red, the underlying mottled pattern structure is still discernible on the dorsal sections.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The specular highlights indicate a hard, glossy, calcified exoskeleton typical of crustaceans.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five pairs of walking legs extend laterally.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple walking legs are visible extending from the body. While not all 10 are perfectly distinct due to overlap and angle, the arrangement is consistent with five pairs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First pair modified into robust claws of unequal size with dark tips.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The two large chelipeds are prominent. They appear robust with reddish/dark tips. Unequal size is common in crabs and plausible here.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Claws have smooth outer surface and serrated inner edges.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The outer surface of the claws appears smooth. The inner edges show textural complexity consistent with serrations, though fine detail is limited by resolution.

The tip of the bottom-most left leg seems to fade into the background or terminate abruptly without a clear dactyl (tip segment), suggesting slight structural incompleteness.
